summary: The Goshen Township Board of Zoning Appeals held a public hearing on two cases. The first was a continued appeal (BZA 2026-002) by Rick Royce/Soda 4 Corporation regarding junk and outdoor storage violations at 1777A Parker Road, which the board denied, upholding the staff's notice of violation. The second case (BZA 2026-004) was a conditional use application by Cincinnati United Soccer Club for an athletic park/soccer training complex at 1456 State Route 28, which the board approved with additional conditions including a solid six-foot privacy fence with deciduous trees along all residential borders and specific lighting restrictions.
decisions: Motion to approve video minutes from June 15th passed 3-0 (2 abstentions, 1 absent)
BZA 2026-002: Motion to deny the administrative appeal by Rick Royce/Soda 4 Corporation and uphold the notice of violation passed 5-0
BZA 2026-004: Motion to approve conditional use for Cincinnati United Soccer Club athletic park at 1456 Ohio 28 with staff stipulations 1-10 plus additional conditions passed 5-0

notes: The meeting had significant transcript corruption/garbled sections. The case number for the soccer complex was referenced as both BZA 2026-004 and BZA 2026-003 in different parts of the transcript. The soccer complex application appears to be a continuation/revision of an approval originally granted approximately five years prior. Mr. Shaw was absent from the meeting. The applicant in the junk vehicle case raised constitutional objections to drone surveillance and property inspections, citing Fourth Amendment rights. Multiple Cedar Lake Lane residents expressed strong opposition to the soccer complex. The board added conditions beyond staff recommendations including a solid privacy fence and reduced lighting levels at the Cedar Lake property border (5 foot candela instead of the requested 25). Next meeting scheduled for August 17th.
